You might want to read the question again.

Project Nevada and World of Pain for NV spring to mind. As does the Mobile Truck Base. Goddamn I love the Mobile Truck Base.

So far, for FO4, Armorsmith Extended is a goddamn staple. As is Crafting Workbenches. No way am I collecting shit off raiders to equip my settlers.
Lowered weapons and craftable ammo are must haves for me.

Street Fighter IV Remix. It makes an overall "meh" entry in the series into an amazing, mad cap experience. Just don't play online with randoms (if you want to play SFIV Remix online, do it with a friend who has the mod.)

Honorable Mention is to Brawl Minus, which does to Brawl what Remix does to SFIV.

Nehrim: At Fate's Edge is a wonderful piece of work. It's a total conversion mod fot Oblivion. Personally I found Oblivion somewhat lacking compared to Morrowind.

This fixes all of my problems, spinning a tale about the sovereignty of man in a world of magic and gods. A fully fleshed out continent without many well thought out and interesting side quests. Fixes to combat make each hit feel like they actually matter. And with no level scaling adventuring feels like adventuring so you may stumble into a cave with a troll twenty levels higher than you and get wrecked.

So you get a great high fantasy RPG that's fully voiced, in German but the English translation is very good. What's not to love?
The long war for XCom: Enemy Unknown/Enemy within.

Lets see in Skyrim SkyUI is a must have for me, even if I'm not using it for other mods requirements just inventory management. I wish there was something like the mod pack launchers for Minecraft for this, would be so cool to play other people's mod setup without having to build each from scratch; and while good Nexus doesn't quite let me choose a pack and it handle downloading and installing 20+ mods that someone else found work together.

Minecraft would be NEI and a map program with location markers, I love the game and the modding community but I am not going to memorize all of their recipies when I am prone to running packs with over 100 mods.

Fallout NV and 3 I would go Fellout as a basic or a more advanced mod that incorporates the same thing.

None of those are game changing but they provide some of the basic features that I have come to enjoy so much I won't bother to play without them.
